title: Encryption: who can decrypt your data, and what must you start for post-quantum?
short: Automate certificate renewal before the 100-day limit on 15 March 2027, and inventory your cryptography for the post-quantum move.
answer: Automate renewal of every public TLS certificate before the maximum lifetime drops to 100 days on 15 March 2027[^br], and make a first cryptographic inventory this quarter so data that must stay secret for ten years or more gets hybrid post-quantum key exchange first. Then judge each encryption measure by two questions: who can use the key, and could you still decrypt if it were deleted?
audience: IT, security and platform teams in EU organizations that run TLS, certificates, disk and database encryption, cloud key management and secrets

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Automate every public certificate renewal by March 2027.
items.text: Public TLS certificates have been limited to 200 days since 15 March 2026, and the limit falls to 100 days on 15 March 2027 and 47 days in 2029[^br]. Renew with ACME, let ACME Renewal Information (ARI) pick the time[^le45] and alert on any certificate a week from expiry.

items.title: Inventory your cryptography, starting with long-lived data.
items.text: List TLS endpoints, certificates and issuers, keys and who holds them, algorithms and trust stores. The EU roadmap calls this a no-regret first step for at least every NIS2 entity, and you can start prioritizing before it's complete[^eufaq].

items.title: Turn on hybrid post-quantum key exchange.
items.text: Traffic recorded today can be decrypted once a large quantum computer exists, so BSI recommends hybrid key agreement for long-term confidentiality[^tr1] and accepts `X25519MLKEM768` in TLS 1.3[^bsitr]. Chrome, Firefox and Apple's version 26 systems already offer it[^chrome][^ffpq][^apple].

items.title: Separate who manages keys from who uses them.
items.text: AWS KMS key administrators can't use a key but can rewrite its policy to give themselves access[^kmspol]. Activate key admin roles just in time with approval, and turn on Key Vault purge protection[^akvsec].

items.title: Get secrets out of code and into a vault.
items.text: Give apps managed identities instead of stored credentials, keep one vault per application and environment[^akvsec], and revoke and rotate any exposed secret at once[^owaspsec]. CI tokens are in the supply-chain sheet.

items.title: Which data must stay secret for ten years or more?
items.text: The EU roadmap counts it as high-risk and wants it protected from quantum attacks by the end of 2030[^euroadmap]. Think of health and HR records, contracts, designs and their backups.

items.title: Where does it travel and where is it stored?
items.text: Follow it through load balancers, VPNs, SSH, APIs, databases and backups, including systems your managed service providers run[^ncscpqc].

items.title: What protects it, and who holds the key?
items.text: Record the protocol and key exchange, the certificate and issuer, where the key lives (HSM, cloud KMS or a file) and who can use it. Load balancer connection logs show the negotiated key exchange[^albpol].

items.title: Which trust stores do your systems rely on?
items.text: Browsers and operating systems update theirs; Java, Go, Python and container images often carry their own. After the eMudhra compromise, Red Hat told customers to rebuild containers on updated base images[^rhsb].

items.title: What can't be upgraded?
items.text: Ask suppliers when they will support ML-KEM. BSI strongly recommends that products expected to run beyond 2030 can be upgraded to quantum-safe methods[^tr1].

blocks.title: TLS baseline
items: **Offer TLS 1.3 and 1.2 only.** BSI prefers TLS 1.3, recommends TLS 1.2 only until the end of 2031 and doesn't recommend TLS 1.0 or 1.1[^tr2].

**Put hybrid groups first.** List `X25519MLKEM768` ahead of `X25519`, as OpenSSL 3.5 does by default[^ossl35]. Windows Schannel supports it but leaves it off; enable it with the ECC Curve Order group policy[^schannel]. On AWS load balancers, pick a policy with PQ in its name[^albpol].
**Meet BSI key lengths.** Use ECDSA keys of at least 250 bits, such as P-256, or RSA keys of at least 3000 bits[^tr1]. The usual RSA 2048 falls short.
**Move SSH too.** OpenSSH 10.0 made `mlkem768x25519-sha256` its default, and 10.1 warns when a connection falls back to a classical method[^openssh].

blocks.title: Who holds the keys
items: **Encryption at rest stops disk thieves, not logins.** It protects against someone who has the hardware but not the key[^azrest]. S3 decrypts for any authenticated request with permission, so stolen credentials read encrypted data as easily as plain data[^s3sse].

**Platform-managed keys are enough for most data.** Microsoft says most organizations can rely on them[^azrest]. Use customer-managed keys where a contract or regulator requires you to control the key.
**A customer-managed key makes availability your job.** Disable it and every read and write to the Azure storage account fails[^azcmk].
**Back up keys you can't recreate, and test the restore.** A restored copy keeps working when you disable the original, so after a compromise rotate and migrate before disabling the old key[^akvsec].
**Rotate wrapping keys automatically, about yearly.** That is AWS's default. Rotation doesn't re-encrypt data or undo a compromised data key[^kmsrot].

blocks.title: Post-quantum dates that set your schedule

items.name: Post-quantum migration
items.scope: EU roadmap milestones. NIS2 entities should at least inventory, map dependencies and analyze quantum risk[^euroadmap][^eufaq]. NCSC, BSI and NIST dates broadly match.

steps.what: Planning and pilots for high- and medium-risk uses started[^euroadmap]
NCSC: discovery done, migration plan ready[^ncscpqc]
High-risk uses migrated[^euroadmap]; BSI's date for very high protection needs[^tr1]
BSI stops recommending TLS 1.2 and classical-only key exchange[^tr1][^tr2]
Medium-risk uses migrated[^euroadmap]; NIST disallows quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms[^ir8547]

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **A certificate authority lost its keys.** In October 2026 eight eMudhra intermediate CA keys proved recoverable. Mozilla removed the emSign ECC Root CA - G3, Chrome committed to the same and eMudhra left the public TLS business[^emudhra]. Update the trust store in every runtime and image (Python: see the secure-python sheet) and keep a second CA set up in your ACME client.

**Public certificates are becoming server-only.** Chrome requires every public certificate issued from 15 March 2027 to be for server authentication only[^crp]. Move mutual TLS and other client certificates to a private CA.

**BSI set end dates for classical cryptography.** TR-02102 version 2026-01 recommends classical-only key exchange and TLS 1.2 until the end of 2031 at most, and classical signatures until the end of 2035[^tr1][^tr2].
**NIST finalized its deprecation schedule.** IR 8547 deprecates every quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithm after 2030 and disallows them after 2035, whatever the key size[^ir8547].

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **Bigger symmetric keys for quantum.** NIST counts approved symmetric algorithms with at least 128-bit security as quantum-resistant[^ir8547], and the EU sees no practical attack on AES-128 in the foreseeable future[^eufaq].
**Post-quantum certificates now.** Classical signatures stay trustworthy until a quantum computer exists, and BSI recommends them until the end of 2035[^tr1]. Key exchange comes first.

**Cloud keys in your own HSM.** AWS says the availability and latency risks of external key stores exceed the perceived benefit for most customers[^xks]. Use them only where a regulator or contract demands it.
**Rotating KMS keys more often.** Wrapping keys are almost never used enough to wear out[^kmsrot].

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Deleting a key something still uses.** A deleted AWS KMS key leaves its data unrecoverable. Disable it first and alarm on use during the 7 to 30 day waiting period[^kmsdel].

**Trusting infrastructure-as-code defaults.** Load balancers created with the AWS CLI, CloudFormation or CDK get `ELBSecurityPolicy-2016-08`, which allows TLS 1.0 and 1.1[^albpol]. Set the policy explicitly.

**Turning off post-quantum key exchange for a middlebox.** Firefox warns that this removes protection against later decryption of recorded traffic[^ffpq]. Some legacy servers can't read the larger handshake[^apple]; fix them instead.
**Hard-coding a renewal interval.** A fixed 60-day renewal won't keep up with 45-day certificates[^le45].

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: Use your host's or CDN's managed certificates, or an ACME client with ARI, and turn on expiry alerts.
Keep the cloud's default encryption, and keep passwords and API keys in a vault, not in code or wikis.
Ask your IT provider and main SaaS vendors when they will support hybrid post-quantum TLS.

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Build the inventory from load balancer logs, certificate transparency and configuration scans, and give every certificate and key an owner.
Enable `X25519MLKEM768` on internet-facing TLS and SSH, and watch connection logs for clients that fall back.
Run a private CA for client certificates and put key admin roles behind just-in-time access.

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: Write the cryptography policy NIS2 requires, with approved algorithms, key management from generation to destruction, and planned reviews[^enisa].
Keep the inventory in a standard format such as CBOM[^euroadmap] and put quantum risk on the board's risk register.
Start with the PKI, the slowest to migrate, and write PQC support into supplier contracts.
